edmund-morrison-augusta-1890-08-16.A1:
AN ATHENIAN SHOT BY A NEGRO.
The Murderer Had Been Reproved for Beating a Mule.
Beating a Mule.
ATHENS, GA., Aug. 16.—News reached here to-night that Henry Hunter, a young man of this city, was shot and probably killed by a negro on the works of the Georgia, Carolina and Northern railroad at Carter's camp, about nine miles from Athens. Hunter, who had charge of the dray line, reproved a negro for whipping a mule until blood came. The negro replied insolently. To-night when work was over Mr. Hunter asked him if he meant what he said. The negro answered by cursing, and drawing a pistol sent a ball through Mr. Hunter's temple. The men who brought in the news said he was unconscious when they left. A posse left here to-night to commence search for the negro. The affair has caused considerable excitement here.
edmund-morrison-augusta-1890-08-16.A2:
HUNTER'S TRAGIC DEATH.
The Death Dealing Bullet Fired While He Was in the Store.
The Death Dealing Bullet Fired While He Was in the Store.

ATHENS, GA., Aug. 17.—Henry Hunter, the young man who was shot last night at Carter's camp by a negro workman, died about 1 o'clock this morning. Parties who visited the scene of the murder last night did not return until nearly daylight. Mr. Hunter was standing behind the counter of the commissary store when the negro, Ed Morrison, walked up to the door and asked him if he meant what he had said at noon. Mr. Hunter replied that he did, whereupon Morrison drew a pistol and shot him and ran. Hunter fell to the floor unconscious, and lingered until 1 o'clock. Dr. D. W. Carter of Smithonia was sent for and did everying possible to save the wounded man.

NATURE OF THE WOUND.

The ball entered the left temple and scattered some of Hunter's brains on the floor.

Messrs. Till and Hart were in the store at the time and were eye-witnesses to the shooting.

Bloodnounds were sent out to the camp last night and put on the track of the murderer, but it was with great difficulty that they followed the trail. At last accounts he was still at large, though being pursued by a posse. Morrison hails from Memphis, Tenn. He is 5 feet 6 inches high, perfectly black and weighs about 130 pounds. He has the look of a burly, determined villain. He wears a black hat, blue overshirt and jeans pants.

Mr. Hunter's remains were brought to the city to-day about 2 o'clock and carried to his mother's residence, on Meigs street. The funeral will occur to-morrow morning.
edmund-morrison-augusta-1890-08-16.A3:
SHOT HIS EMPLOYER.
A Negro Laborer Gets Quick Revenge for His Discharge.

ATHENS, GA., Aug. 18.—Henry Hunter of this city was assassinated Saturday night at Carter's Camp, on the Georgia, Carolina and Northern Railroad, by Ed. Morrison, a negro laborer, at the camp. Hunter had ordered the negro to do something and received an insolent reply, for which the negro was discharged. Saturday night Morrison came into the camp and, walking up to Hunter, shot him in the temple, from the effects of which Hunter shortly afterward died. The negro escaped, but 100 men with blood-hounds are after him, and when captured he will be lynched.
edmund-morrison-augusta-1890-08-16.A5:
HUNTER'S MURDERER CAUGHT.
Sheriff Weir Ran Him Down at Madison and Lodged Him in Jail

ATHENS, GA., Aug. 18.—News reached here this afternoon that Edmund Morrison, the negro who killed Henry Hunter on Saturday night last at Carter's Camp, had been captured near Madison, Ga., by Sheriff Weir of Clarke county and Press Elder. Sheriff Weir left Madison on the 3 o'clock train for Augusta with his prisoner for safekeeping.

SAFE IN JAIL AT AUGUSTA.

AUGUSTA, GA., Aug. 18.—Edmund Morrison, the negro who murdered Henry Hunter at Carter's camp, on the Georgia, Carolina and Northern railroad Saturday night, was put in the Augusta jail for safekeeping by Sheriff Weir of Clarke county to-day. Lynching was feared.
edmund-morrison-augusta-1890-08-16.A6:
AN INFURIATED MOB.
Bent on Lynching a Negro Murderer in the South.
AUGUSTA, GA., Aug. 18.—Edmund Morrison, the negro who shot and killed Henry Hunter at Carter's Camp on the Carolina and Northern railroad, was brought here to-night and lodged in jail to protect him from a mob who would have lynched him. Morrison was employed in a store where Hunter was cletk. Hunter ordered Morrison to perform a disagreeable task, and a few minutes later the negro shot him as he stood behind the counter of the store. Bloodhounds were used in the pursuit of Morrison. Hunter's friends would have then taken the murderer from the sheriff and hanged him if they had an opportunity.
edmund-morrison-augusta-1890-08-16.A7:
CONDENSED DESPATCHES.
The Pith of the News Taken From the Current Events of the Day.
Governor Brackett of Massachusetts, has received the resignation of Chief Justice Morton of the supreme court to take effect Aug. 27th.

A man named William Smith, residing in Griffintown at Montreal, threw his wife down stairs, Sunday night and killed her. He has been arrested.

A fire broke out Monday forenoon in the big double flat on the corner of 32nd street and Fourth avenue, New York. The damage is $10,000. All of the occupants escaped.

Sunday morning, Samuel Jacobson, a prominent business man of San Francisco, was shot in the breast, and fatally wounded by footpads, as he was about to enter his house.

Henry Hunter, of Athens, Ga., was assassinated Saturday night at Carter's camp, by Ed. Morrison, a negro laborer. One hundred men with bloodbounds are after Morrison, and if captured he will be lynched.

About midnight on Saturday, a mob took a negro named Thomas Woodward from jail at Humboldt. Tenn., and hanged him. Woodward was one of three negroes who assaulted and robbed J. A. Greer, last Thursday night.

Frank A. Hosmer of Great Barrington, Mass., has been elected president of the Oahu College, the principal educational institution of Hono'u, and has accepted the position. Hosmer is about 35 years old and a graduate of Amherst College.

A Mrs. Lizzie Lee, a well-dressed young woman belonging at 36th East 15th street, New York, was found lying on a vacant lot on Jersey City Heights, Sunday night, unconscious, exposed to the pelting rain, and had evidently been badly maltreated.

Clarence Ellis, aged 22, of East Somerville, Mass., employed as head brakeman on the Boston ice train between Boston and Dover, was instantly killed at East Kingston, N. H., Monday morning. He was putting a pin on one of the cars when he slipped and fell under the train, the wheels of a number of the cars passing over him. He leaves a wife and family.

One thousand men are out of employment at Lynn, Mass., owing to the moroco-finishers' strike, although the finishers of but one factory alone are directly concerned. It is thought now that the tanners and seamsters will be ordered out by the union, although they are bound by contract not to strike without giving notice and also to work out all stock in soak. The police rather fear some trouble if the strike is not rettled soon.
edmund-morrison-augusta-1890-08-16.A16:
Read THE PLAINDEALER ABOUT PERSONS AND THINGS.
W. G. Louthal, of Newstead, Ky., has been appointed State Superintendent of the Afro-American Farmers' Alliance of Kentucky.

James Bragg, a prominent Afro-American politician and chairman of the Republican Central Council of Mobile, Ala., died at his residence August 18.

Mrs. Myla Powell, a North Carolina ex-slave died at South Bend, Ind., August 16th, aged 106 years. She retained her mental faculties, mind and hearing to the last.

Robert R. Walterman, a barber of St. Paul, committed suicide by firing two shots into his anatomy last Sunday. Meloncholy is supposed to have induced the deed.

Thomas Woodward was taken from the jail at Humboldt, Tenn., August 13 by a mob of white men and hanged to a tree. Woodward was guilty of assault and robbery.

The work of an Afro-American census taker of Nashville, Tenn., was so complete that although two men were sent out by the government to verify his report, no omissions could be found in his territory.

J. E. Rankin, president of Howard University, Washington, D. C., has a thoughtful paper on "The Ethical Training of Afro-American Youth" in the August number of "Our Day." Joseph Cook's magazine.

Frank Morris, a married man residing in Youngstown, O., eloped to Pittsburg with his wife's niece, Miss Sadie Lewis, where he secured a license and was married. Mrs Lewis No. 1 merely says "he cannot live in Youngstown again."

Ed. Morrison, a laborer at Carter's camp near Athens, Ga., shot and killed his employer, Henry Hunter, because he discharged him. Morrison who escaped, is being pursued and if caught will be dealt with after the usual Southern method.

George Early and Bird Woods, two of four men convicted of the burning of the village of Rocky Mount, on the night of October 9, 1889, were hanged at that place August 22. Both men were active Republicans and died protesting their innocence.

A large number of the citizens of Hartford, Conn., gave a reception in honor of Mr. Bolding Bowser, the newly appointed Consul to Sierra Leone last Wednesday. After the banquet and speaks Mr. Bowser was presented with a gold headed cane as a souvenir of his old friends.

Mississippi Republicans at a recent meeting passed resolutions asking the Hon. James Hill, who made the race for Congress at the last election in the third Mississippi district to again submit his name as the standard bearer of the Republicans of the Third Congretsional district for a seat in the Fifty-second Congress.

Mr. H. C. Smith, a Democratic lawyer of Birmingham, Ala., who charged Prof. J. G. Clayton principal of the States school with teaching the children Republican doctrines, was publicly denounced at a citizens' meeting held to endorse Mr. Clayton, whose high character has won for him the respect of the community.

David Johnson, a porter on the Northwestern railroad, who sought to follow in the foot steps of the illustrious Solomon came to grief when he took unto himself wife No. 3. He undertook to chastise her when she reproved him for deceiving her, but she retaliated by having him arrested as soon as she was able to move around.

J. J. Montgomery, the only Afro American delegate to the Democratic constitutional convention in session at Jackson, Miss., was seated Wednesday on a vote of 79 to 28. Montgomery is a full blooded Negro, 45 years of age and presented his case in a speech of thirty minutes, which was followed by applause, a compliment paid no other speaker.

G. H. Smith, grocer, cigar and shoe merchant of Durham, N. C., visited Petersburg, Va., last week, to replenish his stock of cigars. He called at a cigar manufactory and the proprietor thinking that he merely intended making some trifling purchase curtly refused to show his goods, thus losing a big sale, as Smith went elsewhere to buy his stock.

The Ninth Baltimore Colored Ohio National Guard, comprising the entire Afro-American Militia of Ohio, is in camp at Washington, C. H. O. In a dress parade which they gave last week, their work was the subject of much flattering comment, and it is said that should they be called on to do service for the State at any time, they will show themselves to be brave soldiers.

John Henderson, who murdered Gilbert Satterwhite, a prominent farmer near Midway, Ky., last week was taken from jail two days later by a mob and hanged to a tree. An accessory to the murder had been arrested, and has no doubt by this time been hung. The men killed Satterwhite because of their discharge from a threshing machine gang a few days ago. The murderer's friends are highly incensed at the hanging.
edmund-morrison-augusta-1890-08-16.A18:
BOOKED FOR THE GIBBET.
The Negro Who Killed Henry Hunter Sentenced to Lang.
ATHENS, GA., Sept. 4.—Edward Morrison, the negro who shot Henry Hunter of Athens on the works of the Georgia, Carolina and Northern railroad a few weeks ago, was tried for his life to-day in Madison superior court. His trial commenced at 9 o'clock and ended at 2 o'clock, when the jury rendered a verdict of guilty without recommendation to mercy. Judge Lumpkin sentenced Morrison to be hanged on Oct. 17.
edmund-morrison-augusta-1890-08-16.A19:
The Shortest Murder Trial on Record.
A speedy and conclusive trial Friday at
The Shortest Murder Trial on Record. A speedy and conclusive trial Friday at Athens, Ga., was that of Ed. Morrison, the colored man who killed young Henry Hunter, in Madison county, a few weeks ago. Eighteen minutes'argument for the defense, sixteen for the prosecution, twenty for the judge's charge, twenty for the jury, and then the verdict. One hour and fourteen minutes after the evidence closed the jury returned a verdict of guilty. It was one of the quickest trials on record.
